introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2024, ORDINARY LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper. Duration: one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil and an eraser throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Before the examination begins, check that the question booklet is headed "ORDINARY LEVEL - 0520 COMMERCE 1", fill in the information required in the spaces on the booklet and on the answer sheet (Candidate Name, Exam Session, Subject Code and Candidate Identification Number), and do not crease or fold the answer sheet. How to answer: answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. If you change your mind, erase the first mark carefully, then mark your new answer. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all your rough work in the booklet, using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les 50 clés sont déduites du programme O Level Commerce. Clés raisonnées mais discutables, à relire par un enseignant de Commerce : 1 (Manufacturing retenue, bien que Industry soit aussi imprimée), 3 (consular invoice ; la pro forma invoice sert aussi au commerce extérieur), 6 (persuasive advert), 17 (Divisibility retenue comme qualité non requise d'un collatéral ; Accessibility est une autre lecture possible), 20 (D, l'option la plus proche : commission sur la valeur des marchandises traitées), 27 (supermarkets ; les hypermarchés pratiquent aussi le produit d'appel), 30 (B, perte mesurable ; A est vraie de tout risque), 32 (cranes, usuelles dans les ports plutôt que dans les entrepôts), 35 (entrepreneur), 38 (department stores), 44 (air ; les navires de ligne ont aussi un horaire et le chemin de fer n'est pas proposé), 49 (l'option Industry désigne ici la branche extractive ; le mot extractive est absent).

Question 25 laissée en question ouverte : le terme exact (balance of trade, ou visible balance) n'est pas proposé, alors que les autres années du même examen le proposent et rangent trade gap parmi les distracteurs. Options recopiées dans l'énoncé, réponse visée dans le corrigé.

Fautes d'impression conservées dans les options : question 22 (Fascimile, Faxsimile, Faximile sont des orthographes fausses voulues), question 36 (Uberima fides pour uberrima fides), question 20 (Time spend), question 37 (Banks statement). Question 7 : le sujet dit Public Limited Company (certificat de trading) alors que la question 11 porte sur le Private Limited Company (certificat d'incorporation) ; clés déduites du programme.

questions.enonce_markdown: The branch of production concerned with the transformation of goods is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Production is carried out in several branches. The **extractive** branch takes raw materials from nature (farming, fishing, mining, forestry), **manufacturing** changes raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods (for example a factory that turns cocoa beans into chocolate, or a brewery that turns grain into beer), **construction** builds structures, and **commerce** moves goods from producers to consumers.

The branch that transforms goods is therefore manufacturing. Commerce (A) only brings the goods to the buyer, "industry" (B) is a general word that covers extraction, manufacturing and construction, and extractive industry (D) only obtains the raw materials.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Contracts for the carriage of goods by sea are generally known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **charter party** is the contract between a shipowner and a person who hires the ship (the charterer) for the carriage of goods by sea. Contracts of this kind are generally called charter parties; they may be a voyage charter, a time charter or a charter by demise.

A charter by demise (A) is only one type of charter, in which the ship is hired without crew. A time policy (C) is an insurance contract, and a freight note (D) is a document that states the freight charges.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a document used in foreign trade?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **consular invoice** is an invoice for exported goods that is certified by the consul of the importing country in the exporter's country. The customs authorities of the importing country use it to check the value and origin of the goods, so it exists only in foreign trade.

A credit sales invoice (A) is an ordinary home-trade document and a promissory note (C) is a written promise to pay money. A pro forma invoice (D) is a document sent before the sale and it can be used in both home and foreign trade, so it is not the document that belongs specifically to foreign trade.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A quantitative limitation on imports is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **quota** is a fixed limit on the quantity (or value) of a product that may be imported in a given period, for example not more than 10,000 tonnes of rice per year. That is a quantitative limitation.

Tariffs (A) are taxes on imports, so they act on price, not on quantity. "Restrictions" (B) is a general word, and an embargo (D) is a complete ban on trade with a country or in a product, not a limit on quantity.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are invisible items of trade EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Invisible items of trade are **services** that are bought and sold between countries, for example tourism, banking, insurance and air transport (aviation). They cannot be seen or touched.

Petrol is a physical good that can be counted at the customs post, so it is a **visible** item. It is therefore the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of advert that causes impulse buying is associated with;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **persuasive advert** uses attractive messages, slogans and emotions to convince people to buy, often at once and without planning, so it is the type linked to impulse buying.

An informative advert (A) gives facts about a new product, a generic advert (C) promotes a whole class of product without naming one brand, and a reminder advert (D) keeps the name of a known product in the customer's mind.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The legal document needed by a Public Limited Company to start functioning is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A public limited company is first registered, and it receives a certificate of incorporation, which gives it legal existence. It may then offer its shares to the public with a prospectus. Only when the minimum share capital has been subscribed does it receive a **certificate of trading**, which gives it the right to start business.

The memorandum of association (A) and the articles of association (C) are formation documents sent for registration, and the certificate of incorporation (B) is enough for a private company, but not for a public one.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An overcharged invoice is corrected with;
questions.corrige_markdown:
When a supplier has charged too much on an invoice (or goods have been returned), the supplier sends the buyer a **credit note**. It reduces the amount that the buyer owes.

A debit note (C) does the opposite: it increases the amount owed, for example when an invoice was undercharged. An advice note (B) tells the buyer that goods have been sent, and a delivery note (D) goes with the goods.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A banking service that requires regular payments of a specific sum is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **standing order** is an instruction from a customer to the bank to pay a fixed sum to a named person at regular intervals (for example a monthly rent of 50,000 FCFA) until the customer cancels it.

An overdraft (B) and a bank loan (C) are ways of borrowing from the bank. A direct debit (D) is started by the receiver of the money, and the amount may change from one payment to the next.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A sea vessel commonly known as the taxi of the sea is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **tramp ship** has no fixed route and no fixed timetable. Like a taxi, it goes wherever a cargo is available and the shipowner is paid by the charterer, usually under a charter party. This is why it is called the taxi of the sea.

Liners (A, C, D) follow fixed routes on a published timetable, like buses.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Private limited companies only start operating with the issue of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A private limited company cannot offer its shares to the public, so it does not issue a prospectus (A) and it does not need a certificate of trading (D). Once its memorandum and articles of association (B) are registered, it receives the **certificate of incorporation**, which makes it a legal person, and it may start business.

The certificate of trading is the extra document that only a public limited company needs.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The insurance principle that prevents an insured from making a profit out of a loss is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The principle of **indemnity** says that, after a loss, the insurer puts the insured back in the same financial position as before the loss, but no better. The insured therefore cannot profit from a loss.

Utmost good faith (A) requires honest disclosure, insurable interest (B) means that the insured must stand to lose financially, and contribution (D) shares a claim among insurers when the same risk is insured with more than one company.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A payment method where a single cheque is used to make several payments is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **credit transfer** (bank giro) the payer gives the bank one cheque, or one instruction, together with a list of the people to be paid and the amount for each. The bank then credits each person's account. A firm can pay all its employees' salaries in this way.

A standing order (A) is a fixed regular payment, a bank draft (B) is one payment guaranteed by the bank, and a direct debit (C) is collected by the receiver.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The practice of selling goods at lower prices in foreign markets is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Dumping** means selling goods in a foreign market at a price lower than the price in the home market, or even lower than the cost, in order to win the market or to get rid of surplus stock.

Export subsidies (A) are payments by the government to exporters, an embargo (C) is a ban on trade, and tariffs (D) are taxes on imports.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The authority given a bank by its customer to make irregular payments is by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
With a **direct debit**, the customer authorises another person or firm (for example a water or electricity company) to collect money from the account when it is due. The amounts and the dates can change, so the payments are irregular.

A standing order (C) is used for fixed amounts at fixed intervals. A credit transfer (B) and a bank draft (A) are started by the payer for one payment or a list of payments.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the cost of goods is 24,000,000 frs, and rate of trade discount being 20%. Calculate trade discount.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A trade discount is a percentage taken off the list price of the goods. Here:

$$
\text{Trade discount} = \frac{20}{100} \times 24\,000\,000 = 4\,800\,000 \text{ frs}
$$

Option D (3,600,000) would be a rate of 15%, and option C (6,000,000) a rate of 25%.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For a collateral to be accepted, it should have the following qualities EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A collateral is an asset that a borrower pledges to the bank as security for a loan. The bank accepts it if the bank can reach it when the borrower does not pay (**accessibility**), sell it easily to recover its money (**convertibility**), and keep it without losing value, so it must not perish quickly (**durability**).

Divisibility is a quality of money, which can be split into small units. A collateral such as a house, a vehicle or land title does not need to be divisible, so this is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why should a person prefer to invest in a joint stock company?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A joint stock company is owned by shareholders who buy shares. The main attraction for an investor is **limited liability**: if the company fails, the shareholder can lose only the money invested in the shares, and his private property is safe.

Unlimited liability (B) is a disadvantage of a sole trader or a partnership. Decisions in a big company are usually slow because many people take part (C), and a joint stock company is a separate legal entity (D is false).

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: It is not a legal entity.

questions.enonce_markdown: The formula for determining working capital is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Working capital is the money available to run the day-to-day business. It is found by:

$$
\text{Working capital} = \text{Current assets} - \text{Current liabilities}
$$

For example (supposed figures), current assets of 8,000,000 FCFA and current liabilities of 3,000,000 FCFA give a working capital of 5,000,000 FCFA. The other options use items (fixed assets, total assets, all liabilities) that are not part of the working capital formula.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Commission received by agents in trade are usually calculated as a percentage of;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A commercial agent (for example a commission agent or a broker) does business for a principal and is paid a **commission**, which is a percentage of the value of the goods that he buys or sells for the principal. For example, 5% on goods worth 2,000,000 FCFA is 100,000 FCFA. Of the printed options, the value of goods handled for the principal (D) is the closest.

It is not based on the time worked (A), on the principal's profit (B) or on the costs of the transaction (C).

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Time spend to work for the principal.
Value of goods received by principal.

questions.enonce_markdown: Shops with identical buildings selling limited range of goods are called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Chain stores** (also called multiple shops) are branches of one firm in many towns. They look alike (same name, same shop front and layout), they sell a limited range of goods and they are supplied from a central warehouse.

A department store (A) sells many kinds of goods in separate departments under one roof, a supermarket (C) is a large self-service shop, and a hypermarket (D) is a very large self-service shop, usually outside the town.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the full meaning of FAX?
questions.corrige_markdown:
FAX is short for **facsimile**, from the Latin words meaning "make a copy". A fax machine scans a document and sends an exact copy of it over the telephone line to another fax machine. The other spellings (Fascimile, Faxsimile, Faximile) are wrong.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A government department that prevents hoarding of goods is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Hoarding is the keeping of goods in stock to create an artificial scarcity so that the price rises. The government department in charge of **price control** watches prices and stocks in the markets and shops and takes action against traders who hoard or sell above the controlled price.

Town planning (A) controls the use of land and buildings, sanitary protection (B) deals with hygiene, and preventive medicine (D) deals with health.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following features are found in a cheque EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque shows the name of the bank (the **drawee**), the name of the person to be paid (the payee), the date, the amount in words and in figures, the account number and name of the account holder (the **drawer**), and the **drawer's signature**.

The drawee is the bank that pays. It does not sign the cheque, so "drawee's signature" is the feature that is not found on a cheque.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The difference between visible exports and visible imports is called;

*Options as printed:* A) Balance of payments.   B) Trade gap.   C) Invisible balance.   D) Terms of trade.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The difference between the value of the visible exports and the value of the visible imports of a country is its **balance of trade** (also called the visible balance). It is a surplus when exports are greater than imports and a deficit when imports are greater than exports.

The exact term is not among the printed options. The balance of payments (A) also includes invisible items and capital movements, the invisible balance (C) concerns services only, and the terms of trade (D) compare export prices with import prices. "Trade gap" (B) is an informal name for a trade deficit.

**Intended answer: balance of trade (visible balance); the closest printed option is B (Trade gap).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A set of shops with a centralized warehouse is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **multiple shop** is a group of branch shops owned by one firm. The firm buys in large quantities and keeps the goods in a central warehouse, from which it supplies all its branches.

A department store (A), a hypermarket (B) and a supermarket (D) are each a single large shop with its own stock.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Loss leader strategy is common with which of the following shops?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **loss leader** is a popular product (for example sugar or cooking oil) sold at cost price or below it to attract customers into the shop. The shop hopes that they will also buy other goods at normal prices. Supermarkets sell many goods in self-service and customers fill their baskets, so the strategy is typical of them.

Hypermarkets also use it, but supermarkets are the usual textbook example. Multiple shops (B) and department stores (C) rely on other ways of attracting customers.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Using the media to boost a firm's image is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Public relations** are the activities by which a firm builds a good image with the public, for example press releases, sponsorship of a football match, open days and gifts to charities, with the help of the media.

Advertisement (A) is paid publicity for a product, personal selling (B) is face-to-face selling, and sales promotion (D) is a short-term offer such as free samples or discounts.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The department in charge of procurement in an enterprise's purchases is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Procurement means obtaining the goods and materials that the firm needs. The **purchases department** finds suppliers, asks for quotations, places orders and checks the prices and delivery.

The stores department (A) keeps the goods, the production department (C) makes the goods, and the accounting department (D) keeps the records and makes the payments.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A characteristic of an insurable risk is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
An insurable risk must be one for which the insurer can calculate a premium. This requires that the **loss can be measured in money**, that the insured has an insurable interest, and that past statistics exist so that the chance of the loss can be estimated.

Options C and D are the opposite of these conditions. Option A is true of every risk, insurable or not, because a risk is uncertain by nature. Option B is the one that separates insurable risks from uninsurable ones.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mail service for which compensation is paid when parcels are missing or stolen is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
With **registered post** the item is recorded at each stage and the post office pays compensation, up to a stated limit, if it is lost or stolen. It is used for valuable items.

Recorded delivery (A) only gives a proof of posting and delivery, with little or no compensation. Post restante (C) keeps mail at the post office until the addressee comes to collect it, and business reply services (D) let a customer answer without paying the postage.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following facilities exist in a warehouse EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A warehouse uses equipment for moving and stacking goods inside the building: **fork lifts** raise and carry pallets, **conveyors** (belts) move goods from place to place, and **pallet jacks** move loaded pallets over short distances.

Cranes are heavy equipment that is normally found in ports, docks and building sites, where very heavy loads are lifted onto ships or lorries. They are therefore the usual exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following do NOT protect consumers?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Consumers are protected by laws such as a Trade Description Act (which forbids false descriptions of goods), by government services such as the veterinary department (which inspects meat and animal products), and by the consumer movement, called **consumerism**.

**Trade unions** are organisations of workers. They protect the interests of employees (wages and working conditions), not of consumers, so they are the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are used for the classification of an enterprise EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Enterprises are classified according to the **size** (small, medium or large), the amount of **capital**, the **ownership** (private, public or mixed) and the type of activity they carry out (production or trade).

"Variety goods" describes the range of products that a shop may sell, not a basis for classifying an enterprise.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A managerial resource of an enterprise is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The resources of an enterprise are of several kinds. Land (A), labour (B) and capital (D) are the physical and human resources and the financial resource. The **entrepreneur** (C) is the person who organises the business, takes decisions and bears the risks, so the entrepreneur is the managerial resource.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The principle that requires an insured's honesty about a risk is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Uberrima fides** (utmost good faith) requires the insured to tell the insurer honestly every important fact about the risk, for example on the proposal form. If a material fact is hidden or false, the insurer may refuse to pay a claim.

Insurable interest (B) is the financial stake in the thing insured, indemnity (C) limits the payment to the loss, and contribution (D) shares a claim between insurers.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document that gives a summary of a business transaction with the seller is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **statement of account** is sent by the seller to the buyer, usually at the end of the month. It summarises all the transactions of the period: the invoices, the credit notes, the payments received and the balance still owed.

An invoice (A) records only one transaction, a bank statement (B) is sent by a bank, and a pro forma invoice (D) is a quotation sent before the sale.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A retail shop using the services of expert buyers is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **department store** has many departments (clothes, furniture, electrical goods and others). Each department has a specialist buyer, who knows the products and the suppliers and chooses the goods to be sold.

Supermarkets and hypermarkets (A, D) sell mainly in self-service, and multiple shops (C) use central buying by the head office.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which is the most profitable function of commercial banks?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A commercial bank earns most of its income from **lending money** (loans and overdrafts), because it charges interest on the loans at a higher rate than the interest that it pays to depositors.

Accepting deposits (A) is the source of the money that the bank lends, and acting as an agent for payments (C) and issuing travellers' cheques (D) bring only small fees and commissions.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest advantage of sea transport over other forms of transport is that it is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ships can carry very large quantities of heavy goods (crude oil, grain, minerals, containers) at a low cost per tonne, so sea transport is the best for **bulk carrying** over long distances.

It is slow (B is false), it can only go from port to port on fixed routes (C is false), and goods often need to be moved from the port to the destination by road or rail, which means transshipment (D is false).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An account that the holder pays charges to the bank is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **current account** is used for daily payments with a cheque book. The bank does the work of paying cheques and keeping the records, so it charges the holder (ledger fees and other charges), and it usually pays little or no interest.

Deposit, time deposit and savings accounts (A, C, D) are used for saving, and they earn interest for the holder.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A reply to a letter of enquiry is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A buyer who wants to know the price and conditions of goods sends a letter of enquiry. The seller answers with a **quotation**, which states the price, the discounts, the terms of payment and the delivery conditions.

A catalogue (B) may be sent with the quotation but it is not the reply itself. An order (C) is the next step, sent by the buyer, and a statement of account (A) is sent after the sale.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A price quotation of goods right at the manufacturer's warehouse refers to;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **loco** price (also called an ex-works price) is the price of the goods at the seller's premises, in the manufacturer's warehouse. The buyer pays for the loading, transport and insurance from that point.

Ex-quay (B) means that the goods are delivered on the quay at the port of destination. CIF (C) includes the cost, insurance and freight to the port of destination, and FAS (D) means free alongside ship at the port of shipment.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The means of transport that operate strictly on a fixed time table is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Air transport** is operated by airlines that publish a timetable of flights, and they follow it strictly for safety and for the use of airports and runways.

Road (B) and canal (C) transport can be used at any time that the owner chooses. Ships (D) include liners, which follow a timetable, but also tramp ships, which do not, so ships do not operate strictly on a fixed timetable. Railways, which also keep a timetable, are not among the options.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A crossed cheque with the word "And Co": between the parallel lines refers to;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque with two parallel lines across it, with or without the words "& Co" between them, has a **general crossing**. It must be paid into a bank account and cannot be cashed at the counter.

A special crossing (C) carries the name of a particular bank between the lines, so the cheque can be paid only through that bank. An endorsement (D) is the signature on the back of a cheque to transfer it to another person.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Goods bought at 2,000,000 frs were sold at a mark-up of 20%. Determine the gross profit.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The mark-up is a percentage of the **cost price**:

$$
\text{Gross profit} = \frac{20}{100} \times 2\,000\,000 = 400\,000 \text{ frs}
$$

The selling price is then $2\,000\,000 + 400\,000 = 2\,400\,000$ frs.

Option D (500,000 frs) is the profit when 20% is taken as a margin on the selling price, because $2\,000\,000 \div 0.8 - 2\,000\,000 = 500\,000$. That is the common trap, since the question says mark-up and not margin.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document issued by a prospective buyer to many suppliers is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A buyer who has not yet chosen a supplier sends a **letter of enquiry** to several suppliers to ask for prices, discounts and delivery conditions, so that the offers can be compared.

A delivery note (B) goes with the goods, a local purchase order (C) is an order to one chosen supplier, and a letter of credit (D) is a document of a bank used to pay in foreign trade.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following trade restrictions do not raise state revenue EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The question asks which restriction **does** raise revenue for the state. **Tariffs** are taxes on imports that are collected by customs, so they bring money to the government.

Quotas (A) only limit the quantity, an embargo (C) bans trade completely and nothing is collected, and export subsidies (D) are money that the government pays out.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The branch of production concerned with the extraction of raw materials is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The branch of production that extracts raw materials from nature (farming, fishing, mining, forestry, oil drilling) is the **extractive industry**. Among the printed options, only "industry" (D) can mean this branch.

Commerce (A) moves goods to the buyers, constructing (B) builds houses and roads, and manufacturing (C) changes raw materials into finished goods.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a brewery firm offers free bottles to potential consumers, this is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Sales promotion** is a short-term offer that encourages people to buy or try a product: free samples, discounts, coupons and competitions. Giving free bottles to potential consumers is a free sample, so it is sales promotion.

Advertising (A) uses the media to tell people about the product, personal selling (B) is face-to-face selling, and public relations (D) builds a good image of the firm.

**Answer: C.**
